question.text: The main difference between a term sheet and definitive agreements is:

answer.text: Term sheets are filed with SEBI; definitive agreements are not
Term sheets are non-binding; definitive agreements are legally binding
There is no difference; they are the same document
Definitive agreements are shorter than term sheets

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook treats the term sheet (also called the Statement of Principal Terms, SOPT — p.60) as a non-binding first-step document summarising the principal commercial terms. Page 145 states that the term sheet provides "no contractual rights whatsoever" to the parties. The definitive agreements (Share Subscription / Purchase Agreement, Shareholders' Agreement and related contracts — pp.145, 147) are the binding contracts that actually create the parties' rights and obligations. The Trap: Term sheets are not regulatory filings with SEBI, they are not the same document as the definitive agreements, and definitive agreements are typically much more detailed (not shorter) than the term sheet. Note: Source references: NISM Series XIX-A workbook p.60 (term sheet / SOPT as first step), p.145 (term sheet — no contractual rights; definitive agreements as binding contracts) and p.147 (definitive agreements in the deal flow).
